findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure - Confidential files and directory listing via /ftp
findings.description: The endpoint /ftp returns a directory listing of files including backups (.bak), KeePass database (incident-support.kdbx), and confidential markdown documents. Accessing /ftp/acquisitions.md revealed a document marked 'confidential! Do not distribute!' without authentication. This constitutes CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor. The error message for disallowed extensions also leaks server-side file path and Express stack trace (CWE-209). CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
steps: GET http://localhost:3000/ftp/acquisitions.md - read confidential document without auth
findings.evidence: Directory listing included ['quarantine','acquisitions.md','announcement_encrypted.md','coupons_2013.md.bak','eastere.gg','encrypt.pyc','incident-support.kdbx','legal.md','package-lock.json.bak','package.json.bak','suspicious_errors.yml']. acquisitions.md body contained '# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute!'. Error stack trace included fileServer.js path.

findings.title: SQL Injection in /rest/products/search
findings.description: The 'q' parameter of /rest/products/search is concatenated directly into a SQLite query, allowing UNION-based SQL injection. By injecting a UNION SELECT, an unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary data from the database. Demonstrated extraction of all user emails and password hashes (MD5) from the Users table, including admin@juice-sh.op. CWE-89. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
steps: GET http://localhost:3000/rest/products/search?q=' OR 1=1-- -> returns SQLITE_ERROR revealing full SQL query
GET http://localhost:3000/rest/products/search?q=qwerty')) UNION SELECT id,email,password,'4','5','6','7','8','9' FROM Users-- -> returns all users' emails and password hashes
findings.evidence: Query returned: admin@juice-sh.op / 0192023a7bbd73250516f069df18b500, jim@juice-sh.op / e541ca7ecf72b8d1286474fc613e5e45, bender@juice-sh.op / 0c36e517e3fa95aabf1bbffc6744a4ef, and others. SQL error revealed backend query: SELECT * FROM Products WHERE ((name LIKE '%' OR 1=1--%' OR description LIKE '%' OR 1=1--%') AND deletedAt IS NULL) ORDER BY name

findings.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion - 'none' algorithm accepted
findings.description: The application accepts JWT tokens signed with the 'none' algorithm. An attacker can craft a token with an arbitrary payload (e.g., id=1, role=admin) and an empty signature to authenticate as any user, including administrators. The /api/Users/1 endpoint accepted a forged token and returned the admin profile. This bypasses all JWT-based access controls. CWE-347. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
steps: Send GET /api/Users/1 with Authorization: Bearer <token_with_empty_signature> -> returns admin profile

findings.title: [ZAP] Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: [ZAP] Private IP Disclosure
findings.description: A private IP (such as 10.x.x.x, 172.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x) or an Amazon EC2 private hostname (for example, ip-10-0-56-78) has been found in the HTTP response body. This information might be helpful for further attacks targeting internal systems. | CWE-497 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Remove the private IP address from the HTTP response body. For comments, use JSP/ASP/PHP comment instead of HTML/JavaScript comment which can be seen by client browsers.

findings.description: A timestamp was disclosed by the application/web server. - Unix | CWE-497 | WASC-13

findings.title: [ZAP] Session ID in URL Rewrite
findings.description: URL rewrite is used to track user session ID. The session ID may be disclosed via cross-site referer header. In addition, the session ID might be stored in browser history or server logs. | CWE-598 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, put session ID in a cookie. To be even more secure consider using a combination of cookie and URL rewrite.

findings.title: [ZAP] Re-examine Cache-control Directives
findings.description: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached. | CWE-525 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate". If an asset should be cached consider setting the directives "public, max-age, immutable".

findings.title: [ZAP] Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
findings.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797. | CWE-319 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to enforce Strict-Transport-Security.

action.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion - 'none' algorithm accepted
action.description: The application accepts JWT tokens signed with the 'none' algorithm. An attacker can craft a token with an arbitrary payload (e.g., id=1, role=admin) and an empty signature to authenticate as any user, including administrators. The /api/Users/1 endpoint accepted a forged token and returned the admin profile. This bypasses all JWT-based access controls. CWE-347. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
steps: Send GET /api/Users/1 with Authorization: Bearer <token_with_empty_signature> -> returns admin profile
